sources.title: Experimental Null Test of a Mach Effect Thruster
sources.why_relevant: CSUF authors (Fearn & Woodward) report both a positive thrust and a designed null test in which the thrust disappears.
sources.quote: Abstract: "Then we show how this thrust can be eliminated by having two heavy masses at either end of the stack with a central mounting bracket... We find the thrust does indeed disappear in the experiment, as predicted." Full text (Sec. 2.2): "Here we show a clear thrust of approximately 1.5 µN."
sources.geometry_or_result: Measured thrust approximately 1.5 µN in thruster mode (no uncertainty stated); null result: net thrust disappears with equal masses at both ends, as predicted (vibration/systematic check).

sources.title: Experimental Investigation of Mach-Effect Thrusters on Torsion Balances
sources.why_relevant: TU Dresden (Monette, Kössling, Tajmar) replication campaign reporting artifact-level forces and a conventional explanation for Woodward's signals.
sources.quote: Abstract: "It is concluded that the observed effect is a result of coupled vibrations on the torsion balance." Sec. 6: "the forces are much lower than predicted (3 to 30 nN/W), and are present in thruster orientations that should not result in thrust... the effects observed by Woodward using the MEGA drive on a torsion balance can be explained by thermal and vibrational artefacts using Newtonian mechanics."
sources.geometry_or_result: No confirmed uniaxial thrust; observed forces 3–30 nN/W, orders below claimed µN-level forces, appearing in orientations that should yield zero thrust; attributed to thermal and vibrational artefacts.

sources.title: NIAC Phase II Final Report - Mach Effects for In-Space Propulsion: Interstellar Mission
sources.why_relevant: NASA/NIAC-funded CSUF work reporting the force levels measured over the Phase II grant period.
sources.quote: Exec. Summary: "These early devices ... produced on the order of 1µN of force." ... "At this stage we were seeing forces of order 10's of microNewtons." ... "With this free-free motion of the device ... we are regularly seeing 100 µN or so."
sources.geometry_or_result: Reported forces: order 1 µN (early devices), tens of microNewtons (mid-campaign), ~100 µN (free-free sledge design); no uncertainty stated.

sources.title: The SpaceDrive Project - Thrust Balance Development and New Measurements of the Mach-Effect and EMDrive Thrusters
sources.why_relevant: TU Dresden (Kössling et al., IAC-18, Bremen 2018) test campaign reporting no real Mach-effect thrust and attributing signals to thermal drifts.
sources.quote: Results discussion: tests "were performed and indicate thermal drifts instead of real thrusts. This needs to be further investigated."
sources.geometry_or_result: No real thrust observed; measured signals attributed to non-linear thermal drifts rather than thrust.

notes: English-language searches only. Four-source cap reached; all four opened successfully, none paywalled. Opened pages: arXiv abs + PDF, TU Dresden PDF mirrors (Acta Astronautica paper and IAC-18 paper), NASA NIAC PDF. Uncertainty values were not stated in the opened CSUF or NASA sources; geometry_or_result states values exactly as the pages phrase them (orders of magnitude, 'approximately'), not independently validated by me. Mach-effect claims are treated as literature claims only; no propulsion breakthrough asserted.
